title: Video model reproduces pressure estimates but remains limited against catheter measurements
summary: A SlowFast video classifier achieved weighted AUROC 0.854 against cardiologist right-atrial-pressure estimates in 2,618 external ultrasound studies. Against catheter measurements in 319 paired studies, categorical accuracy was 49.5%, compared with 48.9% for cardiologists. This retrospective agreement study does not establish equivalence, clinical benefit or reliable invasive-pressure replacement.
ai_technology: SlowFast R50 convolutional video classifier; learned ultrasound-view classifiers
organization: University of California, San Francisco; California Institute of Technology; Montreal Heart Institute

source_review.scope: Actual primary clinical data selection, patient split, SlowFast model Methods, Tables 1-4 and limitations read; current primary PubMed date and notice metadata checked.

evidence.ai_role: Learned view classifiers select inferior-vena-cava inspiration videos; a trained SlowFast R50 model assigns three pressure categories from their static and temporal features.
evidence.tested: 15,828 archived studies from 11,869 patients were divided by patient into 12,664 training, 1,582 validation and 1,582 test studies. The full test AUROC was 0.823; the abstract's 0.844 refers to a quality-filtered 554-study subset. External evaluation retained 2,618 Montreal studies and yielded weighted AUROC 0.854 against cardiologist categories. All 319 catheter-paired studies were kept in testing; model accuracy against binned catheter values was 49.5%, versus 48.9% for cardiologist estimates.
evidence.unknown: Catheter and ultrasound measurements could be up to 30 days apart. A nonsignificant difference is not an equivalence test. External reference labels were cardiologist estimates rather than catheter measurements, and external image-quality filtering excludes many original studies. Weighted metrics use UCSF class frequencies. Automated scan selection can pick a different video from the one used clinically. No prospective workflow benefit, prevention effect or safe replacement of invasive measurement is established.
